camelback-echo-canyon.note: Echo Canyon Trail closes 8am to 5pm daily under the City of Phoenix Trail Heat Safety Program on days when the National Weather Service issues an Extreme Heat Warning for the Phoenix metro area. No such warning was active as of the August 10, 2026 morning check; the prior warning expired August 9 at 8pm and had not been renewed, so the mandatory program closure is not currently triggered. Forecast highs remain around 107 degrees, so hike before 8am or after 7pm and carry extra water. Source: City of Phoenix Parks and Recreation; National Weather Service.

peralta-fremont-saddle.note: Heat safety advisory: this is an exposed, sun-elevated desert trail in the Superstition Wilderness. The National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for rural Maricopa and northern Pinal counties, including the Superstition Mountains and Apache Junction area, expired August 9, 2026 at 8pm and had not been renewed as of the August 10, 2026 morning check. Tonto National Forest lifted Stage 2 fire restrictions forest-wide on July 20, 2026; Stage 1 fire restrictions (no campfires or charcoal fires outside developed recreation sites, no smoking except in enclosed vehicles or developed sites) remain in effect forest-wide through September 30, 2026, but there is no trail closure here. This trail is inside Lost Dutchman State Park, which has Stage II fire restrictions in effect through October 31, 2026: no wood, charcoal, or open flame, and no smoking on trails. Hike before 8am or after 7pm and carry extra water. Source: National Weather Service; Arizona State Parks.

lava-river-cave.note: FR 171, the access road from FR 245 to the Lava River Cave trailhead, remains closed to motorized vehicles for maintenance (closed since July 13, 2026); reaching the cave requires hiking or biking a longer unpaved approach. Source: Coconino National Forest (Forest Order 03-04-08-26-02).

fossil-springs.note: Heat safety advisory: this trail descends into a canyon. The National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for northern Gila County (below 4000 feet) expired August 3, 2026 at 8pm and had not been renewed as of the August 10, 2026 morning check, though canyon conditions remain hot. A permit is required to park in the Fossil Creek permit area through October 1, 2026, and permits are available seven days a week for the rest of the season. Hike early morning and carry extra water. Source: National Weather Service Flagstaff; Coconino National Forest.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: Heat safety advisory: Grand Canyon National Park continues to urge visitors to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm, when canyon temperatures regularly exceed 109 degrees; this standing advisory follows several heat-related hiker deaths this summer and remains posted on the park's key hiking messages page (last updated August 4, 2026). South Kaibab Trail is fully sun-exposed with no water source. The National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for the Grand Canyon area below 4000 feet expired August 9, 2026 at 8pm and had not been renewed as of the August 10, 2026 morning check, though highs remain very hot in the Inner Canyon. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service Flagstaff.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: Heat safety advisory: Grand Canyon National Park continues to urge visitors to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm, when canyon temperatures regularly exceed 109 degrees; this standing advisory follows several heat-related hiker deaths this summer, including on Bright Angel Trail, and remains posted on the park's key hiking messages page (last updated August 4, 2026). The National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for the Grand Canyon area below 4000 feet expired August 9, 2026 at 8pm and had not been renewed as of the August 10, 2026 morning check, though highs remain very hot in the Inner Canyon. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service Flagstaff.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The North Rim reopened for the 2026 season on May 15 and North Kaibab Trail from the trailhead through Phantom Ranch is open to foot traffic, but the National Park Service advises increased caution near Supai Tunnel and Coconino Overlook due to Dragon Bravo Fire burn-scar hazards, including debris flows, rockfalls, and falling trees. No potable water is available anywhere on the North Rim, including the trailhead and Supai Tunnel; hikers must carry all water needed for the entire hike. Grand Canyon National Park continues to urge hikers to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm due to dangerously hot conditions after several heat-related deaths this summer (key hiking messages page last updated August 4, 2026). The National Weather Service Extreme Heat Warning for the Grand Canyon area below 4000 feet expired August 9, 2026 at 8pm and had not been renewed as of the August 10, 2026 morning check, though highs remain very hot in the Inner Canyon. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park (North Rim status update, July 31, 2026); National Weather Service Flagstaff.
